title: A Simple Skincare Routine for Men
hero_alt: A man in a bathrobe washing his face at a bathroom sink
card_text: Wash, moisturize, sunscreen. A three-step routine for a dry, sunny climate, with a facial as the occasional reset.
lede: A simple men's skincare routine has three steps: wash your face with a gentle cleanser, moisturize, and wear sunscreen during the day. In a dry, sunny place like Carlsbad, the last two matter more than most people think. That's the whole daily routine. Everything else, from exfoliating to serums, is optional, and a facial now and then works as a reset rather than a daily chore.

Here's each step, why a dry climate changes things, and where a facial fits in. This is general grooming information in product types only. For any skin condition, a doctor or dermatologist is the person to ask.

blocks.heading: A gentle cleanser.
paragraphs: Washing removes oil, sweat, dust and yesterday's sunscreen. A gentle cleanser made for faces is the usual choice. Bar soap and body wash can be harsh on facial skin and leave it feeling tight.
Lukewarm water is easier on skin than hot. Pat dry with a towel instead of scrubbing.
Shaving days count too. Washing first clears away oil and dirt, so the razor glides and the skin is ready for lather.
If you work outside or around dust all day, the evening wash is the one that matters most.

blocks.heading: Even if your skin is oily.
blocks.lead: Dry air pulls water out of skin.
paragraphs: Our air is dry for much of the year, and dry air draws moisture out of the skin. A basic moisturizer after washing helps hold onto it. Putting it on while the skin is still slightly damp is a common tip.
Oily skin still does well with a lighter, oil-free moisturizer. Skipping it can leave skin tight in some spots and flaky in others.
Notice how your skin feels by mid-afternoon. Tight and dull means it wants more moisture; shiny and slick means a lighter moisturizer will do.
If you shave, the moisturizer goes on after the shave, once the skin has been rinsed and patted dry.

blocks.heading: The step most men skip.
blocks.lead: The sun doesn't take winter off here.
paragraphs: Southeast New Mexico gets a lot of sun. Daily sunscreen on the face is a standard part of skincare advice, and it applies year round, not only in summer.
Some moisturizers include sunscreen, which turns two morning steps into one.
Sunscreen goes on last in the morning, after moisturizer. On long days outside, sweat and wiping your face take it off, so it needs another layer. A hat with a brim helps, but it doesn't replace it.
The ears and the back of the neck get missed often, and a fresh short haircut leaves more of that skin exposed than you might think.

blocks.heading: Nice, not necessary.
blocks.lead: Add these if you want to.
paragraphs: Once the basics are a habit, some people add:
bullets: Exfoliating once in a while to clear dead skin. Overdoing it irritates.
A lip balm, since lips dry out first in dry air.
Eye creams or serums, if you're curious. They're extras, not requirements.

items.title: Express Facial
items.body: The shorter reset. Massage and warm steam open things up, then a cleanse, a light exfoliation and moisturizer to close.

items.title: Luxury Grooming Experience
items.body: Facial steam and dual hot towels come with the haircut, the beard sculpt, and a wash and scalp massage.

items.q: What's a good skincare routine for men?
items.a: Wash with a gentle cleanser, moisturize, and wear sunscreen during the day. Keep it that simple.
In a dry climate especially. Even oily skin does well with a light one.

items.q: Can I use body wash on my face?
items.a: It works in a pinch, but body soaps are often harsh on facial skin. A face cleanser is gentler.

items.q: How often should men get a facial?
items.a: There's no set rule. A facial works well as an occasional reset or before a big day.

items.q: Can a facial fix acne or a skin condition?
items.a: No. Facials here are grooming, not treatment. See a doctor or dermatologist for skin conditions.
